definition: valid_tool_arguments — a tool call must be CALLABLE against the catalogue the caller supplied. A call is INVALID when (a) its tool_name is absent from `context.tools`, or (b) the tool is present, declares an `inputSchema`, and the call input does not validate against that schema. A call is UNCHECKED when the catalogue entry declares no inputSchema, when Iris declines to compile the schema (see the guard ladder in src/eval/schema-validator.ts), or when the input is larger than the checking limit; an unchecked call is neither valid nor invalid and never fires. An invalid call is RECOVERED when a LATER call to the same tool_name validates; recovery is forward-looking, because an earlier success cannot repair a later failure, and a call to a tool absent from the catalogue is NEVER recoverable — the tool does not exist, so calling it is invented capability rather than a typo. The rule FAILS when at least one invalid call is unrecovered, PASSES when none is (recovered ones are reported in the evidence), and SKIPS when there is no trajectory, when no catalogue was supplied, or when no call could be checked at all. Definitions: src/eval/schema-validator.ts and src/eval/catalogue.ts; rule: src/eval/rules/completeness.ts. Positive = at least one unrecovered invalid call (the rule should FAIL).
source: LLM-authored on 2026-09-05 for arc 4. The catalogue is one four-tool set reused by every case — a read tool with additionalProperties:false, a search tool with an enum and a number, a write tool with a nested object, and one tool that declares no inputSchema — so that a reader comparing two cases is comparing the CALLS and not two different worlds. Cases exercise each clause of the definition: every shape of schema violation, the absent-tool clause, the unchecked clause, and the recovery clause in both directions.
labelling: LLM-authored and LLM-labelled against the documented definition above on 2026-09-05, by reading each trajectory against the definition rather than by running the rule. Each note states which clause decided the label. Cases the measurement then disagrees with are reported as errors, not relabelled. One false negative is accepted by construction and stated here rather than discovered later: an agent that retries with different arguments that are also wrong but schema-VALID scores as recovered, because recovery is defined on schema validity and not on whether the retry was the right call. That miss belongs to no_silent_tool_failure and the completeness bundle, not to this rule.
